abstract_en: An online course on the ethical, legal and social questions raised by data-driven systems, from biased training data to automated decisions in public services.
description_en: Students work through six case studies (credit scoring, recruitment tools, health triage, predictive policing, recommender systems and public registers) and learn to run a lightweight ethical impact assessment. Weekly live seminars are recorded for those who cannot attend; the course is open to students of all disciplines.
learning_outcomes_en: Identify sources of bias and harm in data-driven systems; apply an ethical impact assessment to a real case; explain the main transparency and accountability duties of European regulation; argue a position in an interdisciplinary team.
prerequisites_en: No programming skills are needed. Undergraduates should have completed at least 120 ECTS.
assessment_en: Weekly reflection notes (30%), a group impact assessment (40%) and an individual policy brief (30%). Pass/fail; a transcript of records is issued.
instructors: Lecturer in Data Science|Lecturer in Technology Law
methods_en: Live online seminars, case-based group work and peer review.
remarks_en: Recordings are available for 30 days after each seminar.

abstract_en: A blended course on how warming, changing snow cover and shifting species ranges affect boreal forests, wetlands and coastal waters in northern Europe.
description_en: Online lectures in February and March introduce monitoring methods and climate scenarios. A compulsory field week at the Northvale research station in April lets students sample soil, water and vegetation and analyse the data in mixed groups. A final report links the findings to local adaptation measures.
learning_outcomes_en: Describe the main climate-driven changes in northern ecosystems; plan and carry out a small field survey; analyse environmental data with open-source tools; communicate uncertainty to non-specialists.
prerequisites_en: Introductory ecology or earth science at Bachelor level. Participants must be able to walk several kilometres in uneven terrain during the field week.
assessment_en: Field notebook (25%), data analysis report (50%) and a short oral presentation (25%).
instructors: Professor of Ecology|Research station team, Northvale University
methods_en: Online lectures, a one-week field course and guided data analysis.
remarks_en: Accommodation at the research station is arranged by the host; travel is not covered.

abstract_en: A Blended Intensive Programme in which interdisciplinary teams design a prototype that tackles a social challenge identified with a local organisation.
description_en: Three online preparation meetings in March and April lead to an on-site intensive week in Northvale in May 2027. Teams of students from all four universities of the alliance interview stakeholders, build a prototype and pitch it to a jury of practitioners.
learning_outcomes_en: Frame a social challenge from the perspective of those affected; apply design-thinking methods in an international team; test a prototype with users; pitch an idea clearly and concisely.
prerequisites_en: Nomination by the home university. No specific background is required; teamwork in English is part of the course.
assessment_en: Participation in the online meetings, the team prototype and the final pitch. Pass/fail; a transcript of records is issued.
instructors: Lecturer in Social Entrepreneurship|Innovation coach, Northvale University
methods_en: Online preparation meetings, an on-site intensive week and mentoring by practitioners.
remarks_en: Travel support from the alliance mobility fund is available to students of partner universities.
